description: tell is the Total Electricity Load model developed by the IMMM-SFA project to create spatially consistent electricity-demand projections. It uses multilayer perceptron models trained on weather and historical loads for 54 balancing authorities, then redistributes and scales projections to match annual state-level GCAM-USA demand. Inputs include hourly meteorology and population projections. The Python model outputs hourly demand at county, state and balancing-authority scales across the conterminous United States, in yearly increments through 2100. The repository and detailed user guide are public and the code is free under BSD-2-Clause. These profiles can drive unit-commitment or dispatch simulations and test sensitivity to climate and population change. A limitation is that the documented training uses 2015 to 2019 observations and the model is not immediately portable to another country. County allocation also assumes population-based load shares within service areas. No directly related existing catalogue record was established for the complete model. Documentation was checked without running projections or downloading climate inputs.
inputs: Population projections and annual GCAM-USA state loads
Historical weather and electricity loads for training
